evidence: Met once in the last three years, and the test is softer than the label. Jan 15, 2025: the Commerce Department published an interim final rule that put the weights of the most advanced closed AI models under export licence (ECCN 4E091), which is 'an interim final rule with that effect'. Also, a bill passing one chamber or a proposed rule does not bind anyone, so the test can settle YES with nothing binding in force.
source: Federal Register, 90 FR 4544, Jan 15, 2025: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-15/html/2025-00636.htm
replacement_test: YES if, between Nov 28, 2026 and Nov 30, 2027, a federal statute is enacted, or a federal agency publishes a final or interim final rule in the Federal Register, that limits the release or training of frontier AI models inside the United States (Congress.gov public law record; Federal Register). Bills that pass only one chamber, proposed rules, export-only controls and voluntary schemes do not count. NO otherwise.

Supplier-only stoppages do not count. NO otherwise.

evidence: Each leg was met in the last three years, mostly by things the label does not mean. $1B+ stolen in one cyber event: Bybit lost about $1.5B on Feb 21, 2025 (FBI blamed North Korea on Feb 26, 2025). evidence: Not met by any rule now in force. One older case arguably fits a literal reading: the Commerce Department's Jan 2025 interim final rule put frontier model weights under export licence, took effect Jan 13, 2025 and was dropped in May 2025, so it was on the books for 90 days or more. evidence: The test has no dates, and its second leg was true for most of 2024 and 2025. In current BLS data, information, financial activities and professional and business services payrolls together were 200,000 or more below a year earlier, with total payrolls higher, in every month of 2024 except December (worst: 360,000 below in Apr 2024), in Jan to Mar 2025, Jun 2025 and Dec 2025. The gap has since closed (51,000 above in Oct 2026). The first leg was not met in three years: the NY Fed recent-graduate rate peaked at 5.89% in Oct 2025, was 5.23% in Sep 2026, and was last at 6.0% or more in Jul 2021.
source: FRED USINFO, USFIRE, USPBS, PAYEMS (BLS CES): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/USPBS ; NY Fed, The Labor Market for Recent College Graduates, data updated Nov 2, 2026: https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/college-labor-market

evidence: The named sources will probably not print the figure in time.
